_comment: SecuRAX plugin catalog — the single source of truth for provider plugins. Add a key with `./securax providers`, or by hand in local/compose/.env. The generator (gen_litellm_config.py) turns the ENABLED llm providers into the LiteLLM router config, so each one appears in Chat automatically, still routed through the security gateway. Model IDs change often — override any default with `<ID>_MODEL=...` in .env (e.g. OPENAI_MODEL=openai/gpt-4o). See docs/securax/22-PLUGINS-AND-PROVIDERS.md.

providers.label: Google Gemini
providers.note: Fast, generous free tier: the default for Chat and a build rung. Free-tier prompts may be used to improve Google's products and read by human reviewers (paid tier excluded), so it is Green-tier: the gateway redacts Aadhaar/PAN/card/phone/e-mail before any cloud call, and `./securax residency enable` keeps Red-tier data on the local model. Billing on the same key moves you to the paid terms.

providers.label: Your stronger machine (Ollama on your own PC/Mac, over Tailscale)
providers.note: Lend the estate a stronger machine you own (a desktop with a GPU, a Mac mini): the whole model runs THERE, which is faster than splitting one model across devices. Set REMOTE_OLLAMA_BASE=http://<its Tailscale IP or name.ts.net>:11434 and HOME_MODEL=ollama/<a model pulled there>. Only loopback, private-LAN (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), Tailscale (100.64/10) or *.ts.net addresses are accepted, because this rung counts as 'local' for data residency; anything else keeps it off. See docs/securax/56-POOL-YOUR-MACHINES.md.

providers.label: Local model (Ollama, sovereign)
providers.note: Runs on your box, never leaves it. The sovereign fallback / RED-tier choice.

providers.label: OpenCode Go (open models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)
providers.note: Flat $10/month (Go plan) for open models hosted in the US/EU with zero retention and no training (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: zero-retention agreement renewed monthly, valid through 31 Oct 2026). Sold for CODING-AGENT traffic: SecuRAX uses it only on the build ladder, never for Chat, and only for data you would accept sending to a US/EU cloud.

providers.label: OpenCode Go (open models: GLM Flash)
providers.note: Same OpenCode Go key as above; a second model family so one model's outage does not stop a build.

providers.label: NVIDIA NIM (free, for building only)
providers.note: Free with no card; requests per minute vary by model and load (about 40 is the community figure, not an SLA). NVIDIA's FAQ allows free use for prototyping, research, development and testing, and calls anything else production: building SecuRAX is development, so it is on the BUILD chain only, never in Chat. No published statement on prompt retention: Green-tier only. Another model: NVIDIA_NIM_MODEL=openai/<id> from build.nvidia.com.

providers.label: Cerebras (EVALUATION ONLY: trial credit, not a free tier)
providers.note: Free trial: $5 credit, 30 days, 5 requests/min, payment method required (reported Oct 2026). Not a permanent free tier, and its published data terms do not agree with each other: Green-tier only. It is in NO chain by default; selectable as its own model. With paid credits: ./securax providers chain builder add cerebras.

providers.label: Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI
providers.note: Set AZURE_API_BASE to your endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com) and AZURE_MODEL=azure/<your-deployment-name> (the deployment you created in the Azure portal, NOT the base model name).

providers.label: AWS Bedrock
providers.note: Enable model access in the Bedrock console first. Set AWS_REGION (e.g. us-east-1) and BEDROCK_MODEL=bedrock/<model-id> to pick a model.

providers.label: E2E Networks TIR (Indian cloud, INR billing; PAID, opt-in)
providers.note: Indian provider, GPUs in Indian data centres, INR invoices (UPI/net-banking). Its GenAI API is OpenAI-compatible: set E2E_TIR_API_BASE to the base URL shown for your model in the TIR console and E2E_TIR_MODEL=openai/<model id>. Price per token is on TIR's Usage tab. In NO chain by default. Its zone for data residency is NOT assumed: only after E2E confirms in writing that API requests stay in India, add "e2e-in": "in" to model_zones in governance/residency/IN.json (doc 57).

providers.label: OpenRouter, a strong open model, PAID per use (the Twin's brain)
providers.note: PAID per use: GLM-5.2 about $0.45 in / $3.31 out per million tokens (OpenRouter average, checked 15-Oct-2026). Same key as 'openrouter'. Type yes for OPENROUTER_PRO_OK to accept paid use; the router's monthly max_budget caps spend. Another model: OPENROUTER_PRO_MODEL=openrouter/<id>.

providers.label: Groq (fast, free tier)
providers.note: Very fast inference with a free tier: about 30 requests/min, 1,000 requests/day, 8,000 tokens/min and 200,000 tokens/day per model (Groq's published Free-plan samples, Sep 2026; your account's limits page is authoritative, and limits apply to the whole organisation, not per key). Treat as Green-tier: no Red-tier code without checking Groq's data terms. Free-tier lineups change: if a model 404s, `./securax models` repairs it, or set GROQ_MODEL=groq/<id>.

providers.label: Groq (free tier, second model family: Qwen)
providers.note: Same Groq key as above; a second model family on its own daily quota, so one model's cap or outage does not stop a build. Green-tier only. Another model: GROQ_QWEN_MODEL=groq/<id>.

providers.label: Local coder (sovereign; sized to this machine)
providers.note: Opt-in sovereign coding model for the build chain. Set ENABLE_LOCAL_CODER=1 (`./securax profile` does it), then `./securax pull coder`. The model is picked from `sizing` by the memory Docker can see, and stepped down when it would not fit beside the rest of the estate; pin your own with CODER_MODEL and CODER_MODEL_PIN=1. On a CPU-only laptop expect single-digit to low-tens tokens/s: `./securax bench --models <tag>` measures it. See docs/securax/23-BUILD-WITHOUT-CLAUDE.md.

sizing._comment: Tiers by memory Docker can see (MB). need = file size x runtime_factor (weights + context cache) must fit, leaving reserve_mb for the rest of the estate; otherwise the next tier down is used.

tiers.why: 256K context, best quality per GB (MoE, 3.3B active)
small and fast on constrained hardware

providers.label: ElevenLabs (voice / text-to-speech)
providers.note: Read answers aloud / generate audio with `./securax say "text"`. Not a chat model.

providers.label: Heavy compute (Colab / cloud GPU) — recipe
providers.note: Not a model: the cloud-GPU / Colab recipe. For a machine you own, use the 'home' provider instead (REMOTE_OLLAMA_BASE + HOME_MODEL, doc 56). See docs/securax/22-PLUGINS-AND-PROVIDERS.md § Heavy compute.

chains._comment: Degradation ladders. Each chain is tried in order; only ENABLED providers participate, so a missing key just skips that rung. Every chain MUST end in 'local' (always on) so an answer is possible even with zero keys and zero internet. Paid providers are deliberately absent from bank-assistant (cost guard); the build chain puts Groq's free tier (two model families) right after the OpenCode Go rungs, then cheap DeepSeek. You can reorder the build chain without editing this file: CHAIN_BUILDER in .env (`./securax providers chain builder ...`); local is always kept last. Enforced by tests. 'twin' is the Chat Twin (doc 53): a PAID strong open model first only when you opted in (OPENROUTER_PRO_OK), then the free bank-assistant ladder; DeepSeek is left out because Chat carries personal data. 'home' (your own stronger machine over Tailscale) sits just before the local rungs in every chain: free, private, faster than this laptop.

_reasoning_comment: Optional reasoning cap per provider: set <ID>_REASONING=<level> in .env. Applied only when the provider's CURRENT model matches reasoning.model and the level is listed (checked against LiteLLM's own mapping; on other providers a 'low' effort is mapped to thinking ON or to 'high'). Off by default: nothing changes until you set it. See doc 50.
